statements.t: Management’s Discussion and Analysis is intended to be read in conjunction with the Company’s consolidated financial statements and the integral notes (“Notes”) thereto included in the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025.
The Radersburg property is expected to enhance midstream processing capacity and further vertically integrate the Company’s domestic antimony supply chain.
On March 25, 2026, the Company received approval for three project milestones representing $12.8 million of committed funding for the Thompson Falls, Montana facility expansion.
On April 10, 2026, the Company published an initial assessment technical report summary on its Fostung tungsten project.
The Fostung project was acquired by the Company in 2025 and includes 50 single-cell tungsten mining claims located in the Sudbury District of Ontario.

The Company’s ATO customer base, including the anchor contract customer, has indicated continued demand, and the Company expects ATO shipments to resume to pre-slowdown levels during the fourth quarter of 2026 and into 2027, subject to feedstock availability and seasonality of potential order timing.
Government funding will be accessible to the Company.

We intend to fund our cash requirements with cash and cash equivalents, cash generated from operations, and capital raised from various investment vehicles and believe that cash from these sources will be sufficient to cover our requirements for the next 12 months.
We intend to increase production, reduce costs, and grow revenue profitably by continuing to invest in our employees, customers, infrastructure, and operations.

The Company also continued to expand its domestic critical minerals portfolio through strategic mining claim acquisitions in both Alaska and Montana and, in October 2026, published an Initial Assessment-level Technical Report Summary for its Nolan Creek antimony and gold project located in Alaska, prepared in accordance with SEC Regulation S-K Subpart 1300.

The increase primarily reflects the Company's strategic investment in antimony feedstock and finished products to support anticipated production growth and delivery requirements for both industrial customers and the DLA.
Beginning with this press release, the Company is providing full-year guidance on a sales volume basis and is withdrawing its prior 2026 revenue guidance of $60 million to $75 million.

For full-year 2026, the Company expects to sell approximately 1.68 million to 1.81 million pounds of antimony, compared with approximately 1.41 million pounds in 2025, an increase of approximately 24% at the midpoint.
The Company also expects to sell approximately 17,500 to 18,500 tons of zeolite in 2026, compared with 14,114 tons in the first nine months of the year and 1,319 tons in October 2026.
The Company’s guidance assumes that, at most, lots TF-8 and TF-9 are accepted before December 31, 2026, and that lots TF-10 through TF-14 are accepted in 2027.
The Company expects average cost per pound to continue to benefit from lower feedstock costs and from higher throughput as utilization of the expanded Thompson Falls smelter continues to increase.

Underlying government and industry demand for domestically sourced antimony remains robust, and the Company continues to expect the DLA IDIQ contract to be a meaningful long-term revenue contributor, as the only company qualified to meet such order demand.

As Thompson Falls capacity utilization continues to increase, in combination with the Company’s new processing capacity at Radersburg and improved processing at the Company’s Mexican operations, the Company expects to further expand the volume of antimony products it can supply to both government and industrial customers in 2027 and beyond.
That pace was slower than we anticipated back in August, when we expected $9 to $10 million of DLA revenues during the third quarter.
These were the first deliveries under our new exclusive contract, and every step — sampling, assay, shipment, inspection and acceptance — took longer than originally anticipated.

Since then, we have cut the time from sampling to payment from as long as 124 days to about 70 days, and while the timing of each approval and acceptance ultimately rests with the DLA, we expect the process to continue to become more routine as we move into fiscal year 2027.

With antimony prices down more than 60% from a year ago, and revenue timing tied to government acceptance dates, we are moving to volume-based guidance beginning today, which better reflects what we do control — producing and delivering antimony.
We expect to sell 1.68 to 1.81 million pounds of antimony in 2026, up about 24% from 2025 at the midpoint, and October was our highest monthly sales volume, with more than 310,000 pounds sold.

While antimony prices have declined from the historic elevated levels seen in 2025, we have continued to secure feedstock and build inventory to support expected customer demand at prices that allow meaningful gross margins.
As we advance Nolan Creek and Fostung Tungsten, we expect both gold and tungsten to become an increasingly important part of our business.
As mining of these minerals from our new projects are produced and sold, investors will see it reported within a separate precious metals revenue line item.
A replay of the conference call and the transcript will be available in the Investors section of the Company's website at https://www.usantimony.com/investors .
These statements are based on current expectations, estimates, forecasts, and projections about the industries in which the Company operates, as well as management's beliefs and assumptions.

Based on our current production and delivery schedule, we anticipate completing our first delivery order of $9.9 million nearly one year ahead of schedule.

risks.t: fluctuations in the market prices and demand for antimony and zeolite
delays in the sampling, inspection or acceptance of shipments by the DLA
the risk that the assumptions underlying the Company’s full-year 2026 sales volume guidance prove incorrect
the availability, quality, and cost of third-party antimony feedstock, including deliveries from the Company’s partner in Bolivia
volatility in the market value of, and currency exposure relating to, the Company’s investment in Larvotto Resources Limited
dilution and other effects of the Company’s equity issuances
changes in domestic and global economic conditions
operational risks inherent in mining and mineral processing
geological or metallurgical conditions
availability and cost of energy, equipment, transportation, and labor
the Company’s ability to maintain or obtain permits, licenses, and regulatory approvals
changes in environmental and mining laws or regulations
competitive factors
the impact of geopolitical developments
the effects of weather, natural disasters, or health pandemics on operations and supply chains
